newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit firms on corporate, offshore dollar sales.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit firms on corporate, offshore dollar sales.

text.p: * Ringgit firmed on dollar sales by local corporates and offshore players
* Sentiment helped by reports that Malaysia appears to favour a stronger ringgit
The ringgit firmed against the dollar in early Asian trading on dollar sales by local corporates and offshore players, dealers said.

"There were a lot of sell orders out of Kuala Lumpur around 2.5150. Offshore players also sold the dollar," said a European bank dealer in Kuala Lumpur. "Dollar/ringgit went all the way down to 2.5110."
But profit-taking provided support for the dollar at 2.5120, dealers said.
They said the ringgit might test the 2.5100 level through the day and a possible minor break to 2.5080.
Some dealers said ringgit sentiment was helped by reports that Malaysia appears to favour a stronger local currency.

Local newspapers quoted acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim as saying late on Thursday that the spillover effect of the Thai baht on the ringgit was temporary and can be controlled within a short period.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the context of the ringgit and the baht, and the economic fundamentals in Malaysia and Thailand were different.
At 0230 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5130/40 a dollar against 2.5160/65 at close in Kuala Lumpur on Thursday.
Dealers said dollar's upside was likely to be capped at 2.5150 for the day.
